summary: The study describes the growth behavior of plasma enhanced atomic layer deposited (PEALD) ruthenium (Ru) thin film as a copper diffusion barrier. The Ru layer was grown on bare Si and a 30 nm bottom wide nano-patterned trench with an aspect ratio of 4. The process parameters were precisely controlled, resulting in a uniform Ru film layer at 8-inch full wafer scale with a growth temperature of 290 /C176C and 230 mTorr of working pressure. The growth rate was saturated at 0.35 Å/cycle for TaN and 0.33 Å/cycle for Ru. The conformity was measured to be 0.86 on Si and 0.97 on the TaN/Si trench, indicating excellent step coverage. The physical properties of the Ru/TaN bilayer showed a dense amorphous phase Ru thin film layer successfully grown using PEALD.
evidence: The growth behavior of plasma enhanced atomic layer deposited (PEALD) ruthenium (Ru) thin film was systematically studied in the context of its application to a copper diffusion barrier. The Ru layer was grown on bare Si and a 30 nm bottom wide nano-patterned trench with an aspect ratio of 4. Bis(ethylcyclopentadienyl)ruthenium [Ru(EtCp)2] was used as a precursor and NH3 was used as a plasma enhanced reactant. The process parameters were precisely controlled, resulting in a uniform Ru film layer at 8-inch full wafer scale with a growth temperature of 290 /C176C and 230 mTorr of working pressure. The growth rate was saturated at 0.35 Å/cycle for TaN and 0.33 Å/cycle for Ru. The conformity was measured to be 0.86 on Si and 0.97 on the TaN/Si trench, which indicates excellent step coverage. The physical properties of the Ru/TaN bilayer studied by X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed that a dense amorphous phase Ru thin film layer was successfully grown using PEALD.
